evidence: namespaceOf calls mod.evaluate() and returns without awaiting or catching; a module body rejecting after its first await produces an unhandled rejection, which node terminates on by default, so the failure bypasses the entry try/catch that is the only path onto the boot channel.
guidance_note: A promise started and deliberately not awaited needs its terminal handler attached at the point it is started, not inherited from a caller that has already returned.

evidence: decode() did byName.get(p).bytes().toString(enc) with the CALLER's encoding while the container record carries its own declared encoding; bun-graph.test.js already had a utf16le text asset, so fs.readFileSync(p,'utf8') would return mojibake.
guidance_note: When replacing a caller-supplied encoding with a stored one, enumerate what that parameter can carry first: text decodes and byte transcodes ('hex','base64') are different requests and only one of them wants the stored encoding.

evidence: SEAMS.md documents byte_count as u64 at offset +0 and OFFSETS.modulesOffset=8 reserves eight bytes for it, but at() reads every field with readUInt32LE, so the high half is discarded silently rather than refused.
guidance_note: Read each container field at the width the format record states, not the width today's data happens to fit in; a narrower read is a guess in a parser whose whole contract is refusing guesses.

evidence: Every other member of the Bun.file(p) object goes through readAny/existsAny/statAny, and stream() alone calls fs.createReadStream(p) on the real disk, so an embedded /$bunfs/ path throws ENOENT.
guidance_note: When a facade object routes N members through one dispatch, check every member against that dispatch before shipping; one member written straight through is the whole abstraction's hole.

evidence: Duplicate of F4 from the same round: same stream() line, same ENOENT consequence; the agent's reply says 'Same as the stream() thread above; one fix'.

Buffer.from(data.buffer ?? data) takes the whole backing ArrayBuffer, and this codebase's own record.bytes() is buf.subarray(...) into the 199MB executable buffer, so Bun.write of an embedded slice would write hundreds of megabytes from the wrong offset.
guidance_note: Define one bytes-from-a-caller-value helper the first time you need it; the second ad-hoc Buffer.from is where the same view-window bug comes back (it did, in F36/F40).

evidence: meta.require special-cased loader==='text' only, so a napi or file record fell through to namespaceOf -> new vm.SourceTextModule(record.text()), feeding latin1-decoded native bytes to the JavaScript parser; the loader field exists precisely to prevent that.
guidance_note: When a record carries a discriminant, dispatch on every value of it in one place; handling one arm and defaulting the rest re-introduces the sniffing the discriminant was added to remove.

evidence: The eager link loop sat outside the try/catch that wraps entry.evaluate(), so a rejecting externalModule() import would crash with no report(); the agent said it was already fixed in the working tree, and the round-1 and round-2 diffs show linkAll()/evaluateEntry() sharing one try/catch, so the claim held.

One `reported` flag guarded both 'painted' (fired on every stdout write) and the terminal boot-threw/absent messages, so any post-paint crash message was dropped; the round-1 code shows the split the agent claimed - report() for the one-per-process verdict, send() for boot-threw.

The verdict was formed in child.on('exit'), which fires when the OS reaps the child and can precede delivery of the last boot-channel chunk, so a plan that painted and exited immediately reads as never painted and gets re-run - the double execution the file says must never happen.
guidance_note: A verdict assembled from two independent event sources must wait on both sources ending, never on whichever fired first.

evidence: child.stdio[BOOT_FD].on('error', () => {}) discards a genuine channel read error, and the resulting reason says only 'nothing painted within Nms' - the same function's comment claims the degrade is never quiet.
guidance_note: An empty catch or handler in a file whose stated job is naming failures is a contradiction the author can find without a reviewer; grep your own diff for `() => {}` and `catch {}` before pushing.

evidence: Duplicate of F3, same byteCount u32 read; the agent replied 'Same defect as the byteCount thread above; fixing once'.
SEAMS.md stated '1,640 JS chunks' in one section and '1,642 code-split chunks' in another for the same graph; both are copies of a number bun-host.mjs computes from graph.modules.
guidance_note: A count written into prose is a second copy of a fact the code already computes; either derive it or omit it, because it drifts on every push (it drifted again in F97).

evidence: The doc's '15' was stale, so the drift was real, but the reviewer's counted replacement (18) was also wrong - the agent's fix landed 20/12/16/22, so neither the old nor the proposed number matched the files.
guidance_note: Recount every stated test total from the files in the same commit that adds tests; the number is stale the moment a suite grows.

evidence: Third instance of the byteCount u32/u64 mismatch in one round; the agent replied 'Same defect as the two byteCount threads above; one fix covers all three'.

Both `trailerAt === -1` and `offsets < 0` returned ABSENT.noTrailer, so a file that DOES contain a trailer but has no room for the offsets struct reports 'no trailer found' - false, and indistinguishable to the caller the module says switches on reason.
guidance_note: One reason code per distinguishable cause; reusing an existing code for a second condition lies to the caller that the module's own comment says switches on it.

evidence: readdirSync on an embedded path fell through the {...real} spread to the real fs and raised a bare ENOENT; the agent refused to synthesise a directory listing (a fabricated answer) and instead wrapped every function of the real module to refuse embedded paths by name, which is the stronger fix.
guidance_note: Closing a gap 'as a class' means writing the accept/reject table for the whole class first - nested objects (F33), callback-shaped members (F34), constructors (F71/F87) and directory-prefix paths (F98) were each a separate later round of this same wrapper.

evidence: wyhash: () => 0n returns the same constant for every input while being a present key, so the Proxy's absent-API recording never fires; a present-but-wrong stub is exactly what this file's own header argues is worse than absence.
guidance_note: A stub that returns a constant is a wrong answer forever; decide at write time between a real implementation and a recorded absence, and never write the third thing.

evidence: Bun.spawn accepts both spawn(cmd[], options) and spawn({cmd: [...], ...}); the shim did cmd[0]/cmd.slice(1) unconditionally, so the object form throws 'cmd.slice is not a function'.
guidance_note: When reimplementing a documented API, enumerate its call shapes from its own type definitions - bun-types is installed on this machine and lists them.

evidence: The row loop validated name prefix, bounds, encoding and loader but not uniqueness, and the sole consumer builds new Map(modules.map(m => [m.name, m])), so a duplicate silently makes one module unreachable instead of producing the typed absence this parser promises.
guidance_note: A parser that hands its output to a keyed collection owes a uniqueness check; the collision is invisible at the parse site and silent at the consumer.

evidence: which() ran spawnSync('command', ['-v', cmd], {shell:true}), which joins into /bin/sh -c with no quoting, so a name containing ';' executes; the real Bun.which is a PATH scan with no shell at all.
guidance_note: shell:true on a value that came from anywhere but a literal is command injection; reimplement the no-shell semantics rather than escaping into a shell.

evidence: bun-host.mjs carried the decode dispatch, the loader dispatch, the linking machinery and the report guard with no test file at all, and the same round found several bugs in exactly that logic by reading - the agent called it the most useful finding in the review.
guidance_note: Extract the parts with logic into modules with factories and suites while writing them; the wiring file is the only thing that should ship untested, and deciding that after review costs the rounds it cost here.

evidence: TERMINAL_RESET sends only ANSI sequences (alt screen, cursor, bracketed paste, SGR); raw mode is a tty line-discipline property set via setRawMode/termios and survives the process, so the comment's promise that no plan can leave the terminal owning raw mode was false.
guidance_note: When a comment promises a guarantee, check the mechanism actually reaches it; here the escape codes and the termios state are different subsystems.

evidence: meta.require fell through to createRequire(import.meta.filename) for any non-embedded specifier, so a chunk requiring 'fs' got node's real fs rather than the embedded-aware substitute the import path receives, breaking SEAMS.md's claim that the substitution is transparent.
guidance_note: When two entry points resolve the same names, route them through one resolver rather than surveying today's call sites; the agent's own reply says the guarantee should hold by construction rather than by survey.

evidence: report(`boot-threw ${e && e.message}`) yields the literal 'boot-threw undefined' for a thrown string or plain object, which is the silence the channel exists to prevent.
guidance_note: Anything reachable by `throw` can be a non-Error; stringify at the one point where a thrown value becomes a message.

evidence: The header lists two exits that are never re-run (a clean exit, any exit outside a tty) unconditioned on painting, but the code returned booted:false on !paintedAt before reaching either check, so a silent one-shot that exits 0 gets re-run by the next plan - the double execution the comments forbid.
guidance_note: When a header states a rule list, its order is part of the contract: write one test per stated exemption rather than trusting the branch order to match the prose above it.

evidence: escapeHTML: (s) => String(s) escapes nothing, so hosted code that believes it sanitised a value embeds raw input; it is a present key, so the absent-API Proxy never records it.

CryptoHasher forwarded any algorithm name to crypto.createHash, and Bun's supported set (verified in bun-types: blake2b256, sha3-*, shake*, md4, ripemd160) includes names node does not serve, so the constructor throws an opaque error from a call site outside the boot try/catch.
guidance_note: A pass-through to a foreign API needs the accept/reject set written explicitly; the mapping table this fix introduced then produced its own wrong answer (F30).

evidence: deepEquals via JSON.stringify makes key order significant, so {a:1,b:2} and {b:2,a:1} compare unequal, and NaN/Map/Set/undefined-valued properties all mis-compare - wrong for a primitive whose only job is that question.
guidance_note: A from-scratch structural-equality function needs its accept/reject table written before the first line: RegExp (F56), cycles (F65), Error (F99), boxed primitives (F110), Set members (F111) and Map keys (F123) each cost a separate review round here.

evidence: Verified in bun-types that blake2b256 is a real Bun algorithm and node has no blake2b256; blake2b's digest length is mixed into its IV, so NODE_ALGORITHM mapping it to blake2b512 returns a different function's bytes. Before F28's fix createHash('blake2b256') threw loudly; the fix turned that into a silent wrong digest.
guidance_note: A compatibility mapping table must map only names that are the SAME function; a 'closest available' entry converts a loud failure into a silent wrong answer.

evidence: Bun.serve returned a fake server object that never listens, so a caller awaiting an OAuth callback waits forever while key-in-target keeps the absent-API Proxy silent; the agent checked the graph, found a real fetch/.unref/.stop(true) call site, and implemented it over node:http. The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here: this stub is verbatim from the pre-review bun-host.mjs (visible in F17's round-0 hunk) and was only relocated into bun-surface.js by the F22 fix.

Bun.color(input, format) converts between colour representations; the identity stub returns '[object Object]' for an object input. The agent surveyed the graph, found no call site, and deleted it so an absence is recorded. Flag false positive: the identity stub is unchanged pre-review code moved into the new module.
guidance_note: Survey call sites for every member of a compatibility surface once, at authoring time, and delete the ones nothing reaches - the same survey then answered F51, F60 and F67 in later rounds.

evidence: substituteFor skips non-function properties, and node's fs.promises is an object, so it survived the {...real} spread unwrapped and require('fs').promises.readFile(embeddedPath) reached the real fs - the class-wide closure the F17 fix advertised did not reach nested objects.
guidance_note: 'Wrap every function of the module' is not 'wrap every reachable entry point': enumerate the module's shape (functions, nested namespaces, constructors) before claiming a gap is closed as a class.

evidence: The reviewer is right that node's callback-style fs never throws synchronously for a path error, so ordinary fs.readFile(p, cb) code is not wrapped in try/catch. The agent's counter is sound on its own terms and consistent with the module's stated design: a callback error is a value the app catches and turns into 'asset missing', which is the laundering the refusal exists to prevent. The final code confirms only the promises substitute rejects; everything else throws.

createReadStream: (p) => streamFrom(bytes(p)) drops the second argument, so {start,end} or {encoding} silently yields the full raw asset - the F4 fix routed stream() through the embedded fs without carrying the options the real API takes.
guidance_note: When you route a member through a new implementation, carry its full signature across; a dropped optional argument is a silent wrong answer, and this one took three more rounds (F58, F64, F107) to actually land.

evidence: fnv1a64 and crc32 both do Buffer.from(input.buffer ?? input) - the exact view-window bug F6 had just been fixed for via asBuffer, in the same push, in the same file; record.bytes() returns a subarray into the whole-executable buffer, so hashing an embedded record would walk ~200MB.
guidance_note: After fixing a bug class, grep the whole diff for the pattern before pushing; the sibling here was written in the same commit as the fix.

evidence: Duplicate of F30 raised in the same round with the same blake2b truncation argument; the agent replied 'Same fix' and removed the mapping table entirely.

bytes(p) handed back bun-graph's live subarray into the one buffer holding the whole executable, while real readFileSync always returns memory the caller owns, so hosted code writing into what it read edits the graph. Flag false positive on causation: round 0's decode() returned the same view; the module move did not create it.
guidance_note: A read API that hands back a view into shared memory has to copy, because its contract is the real fs's contract and that one gives the caller ownership.

evidence: Bun names stdin/stdout/stderr at the top level and node only understands options.stdio, and node silently ignores unknown keys, so an 'ignore' became an unread pipe that fills and blocks the child. The agent confirmed the graph passes exactly stdout:'pipe'/stderr:'ignore' and then awaits child.stdout.text(). Flag false positive: round 0 forwarded options unchanged in the same way; the F19 fix only added the object call form.
guidance_note: Translating an option bag between two APIs means enumerating both vocabularies; silently-ignored keys are the failure mode that produces a hang with no cause.

evidence: Duplicate of F36 in the same round, naming asBuffer explicitly as the fix already present a few lines below.

Bun.write returns Promise<number> of bytes written (confirmed in bun-types); the shim returned a constant 0, so a caller checking for a short write is told nothing was written. Flag false positive: identical in round 0's bun-host.mjs.

The Proxy returned () => undefined for an unknown key, which is truthy, so `if (Bun.newApi)` takes the present branch - the doctrine one level up from the stub's return value. Flag false positive: the same Proxy body is in round 0's diff.
guidance_note: Feature detection reads truthiness, so an absent member has to be undefined; a callable placeholder is a present-but-wrong stub wearing a different hat.

evidence: The F22 fix extracted embedded-fs.js and bun-surface.js but left the linking machinery, the loader dispatch and the report guard - the riskiest logic in the file - untested; the agent agreed and extracting bun-runtime.mjs immediately exposed a latent bug (the up-front link loop only worked because Bun emits its table dependencies-first).
guidance_note: When a finding says 'this logic is untested', check the extraction covers the logic the finding named, not the parts that were easiest to lift out.

evidence: VIRTUAL_ROOT = '/$bunfs/' was restated in the new embedded-fs.js while bun-graph.js already defines it; both files are new in this PR, so the duplication was created by the extraction rather than inherited.
guidance_note: When splitting a file, import shared constants from the module that owns the format rather than re-typing the literal into the new file.

evidence: F26's fix moved `exit === 0 || !interactive` to the front of verdict(), which is precisely what made a named refusal with nothing painted return booted:true in a pipe - so a graph the host cannot read produced neither a fallback nor a log. The reviewer's own best finding of round 0 created this one.
guidance_note: Reordering guard clauses changes what every later clause can see; when you promote a condition, re-derive each remaining branch's reachability rather than assuming the set of outcomes is unchanged.

evidence: The quoted 'verified live' transcript predates the absent-api diagnostic added in the same PR, so re-running the break test could not produce the quoted string; both the transcript and the feature were in the original push, so the flag is a false positive on causation.
guidance_note: A quoted transcript is a test result with no runner; re-run it in the commit that changes what it prints, or do not quote it.

evidence: SEAMS.md and bun-host.mjs's header both claimed every degrade leaves on the boot channel named, while only two paths funnelled into send() and no uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handler existed; the reviewer offered add-handlers or narrow-the-claim and the agent narrowed the doc.
guidance_note: When a claim is stated in two files, a fix that edits one leaves the other false - F84 re-raised the identical claim from bun-host.mjs's header two rounds later.

evidence: entryIndex was bounds-checked but the entry row's loader was not, so a graph whose entry points at a napi/text row returned ok:true and failed later as an ad-hoc throw in the host, bypassing the parser's own ABSENT taxonomy; the agent notes the new check caught one of his own fixtures immediately.
guidance_note: A parse boundary that promises 'callers cannot receive a bad record' has to prove the properties its consumers rely on, not only the ones needed to finish parsing.

evidence: Bun.hash and hash.wyhash take an optional seed (confirmed in bun-types); fnv1a64 was written by the F18 fix with a single parameter, so Bun.hash(x,1) and Bun.hash(x,2) return the same value. The agent notes writing the test caught that the wrapper still dropped the seed after the underlying function took one.
guidance_note: Reimplementing an API member means reproducing its full signature; an ignored optional argument silently collapses the distinctions the caller asked for.

evidence: sleepSync: () => {} returns instantly from the one call whose entire purpose is not to; the agent implemented it with Atomics.wait. Flag false positive: identical line in round 0's diff.

Bun.stdin/stdout/stderr are BunFile-like in real Bun, and the shim exposed the raw node streams, so await Bun.stdin.text() throws. The agent surveyed the graph, found no reference to any of the three, and deleted them so a future reach is recorded as an absence - a better answer than a hand-written BunFile wrapper nothing exercises. Flag false positive: the three raw streams are unchanged round-0 code.

F7's fix gave requireSync the loader-aware dispatch and left link()/evaluatedModule() checking only loader==='js', so an embedded text/file/napi specifier reached externalModule and was refused with 'neither embedded nor a module this host provides' - false, since the graph does name it.
guidance_note: When a dispatch rule is discovered for one entry point, apply it to every entry point that resolves the same names in the same commit; the agent's 'one dispatch' reply here turned out to be structural only and F63 re-raised it.

evidence: F24's fix added a second, sync external cache, and provided.ws is a factory that defines class Server inside its body, so the sync and async caches each called it once and got different constructors - an instanceof check across the two paths fails.
guidance_note: A provider invoked once per resolution path must be built once, not per call; adding a second cache alongside an existing one duplicates every value it holds.

evidence: `else if (line) refusal = line` is last-write-wins, and namespaceOf's fire-and-forget catch can send several boot-threw lines, so the root cause was overwritten by whatever followed it; the reviewer suggested accumulating a list and the agent kept the FIRST refusal instead, which answers the actual complaint more cheaply.
Duplicate of F52 in the same round, arguing the text-loader case specifically; the agent replied 'Same fix: the two callbacks share one dispatch'.

The replacement deepEquals falls through to own-enumerable-key comparison for RegExp, whose source and flags are prototype getters, so Object.keys(/abc/) and Object.keys(/xyz/) are both [] and two unrelated regexes compare equal.
guidance_note: An equality function's fallback branch is only safe for objects whose whole state is enumerable own keys; list the built-ins that violate that before writing the fallback.

evidence: The hand-rolled t() harness written for the new suites calls fn() and increments pass without awaiting, so the async case printed ok whatever it asserted; fixing it immediately exposed a real failure that had been green (the promises substitute threw synchronously instead of rejecting).
guidance_note: A hand-rolled test harness must await the case function, and you prove it by making a case fail on purpose before trusting a green run.

evidence: F35's fix added the options parameter at the call site (streamFrom(bytes(p), options)) while the only production streamFrom in bun-host.mjs was (bytes) => Readable.from(bytes), which ignores it; the test asserted forwarding to a stub echo, so it passed on the half-fix. The agent's own words: 'my last-round fix was half of one'.
guidance_note: A fix that threads a parameter has to be verified at the receiving end, not the sending end; a test that stubs the receiver proves only that the caller changed.

evidence: serveOver, written by the F31 fix, passes an async listener to http.createServer with no try/catch, so a throwing fetch handler leaves the request hanging and the rejection unhandled, which under node's default terminates the process for one bad response.
guidance_note: Every async function handed to a callback-based API needs its own try/catch, because the API will not await or catch the promise it gets back.

evidence: Bun.spawnSync returns exitCode/signalCode/success where node returns status/signal, so destructuring gives undefined and `if (result.success)` is always false; F39's fix added withBunChildShape for the async path and left the sync sibling unadapted. The agent surveyed the graph, found no call site, and deleted the member. Note the thread also carries a reply ('a promise nobody awaits takes the process down') that belongs to F78.
guidance_note: When adapting a return shape for one member, check the sibling member with the same contract in the same commit.

evidence: Verified in bun-types on this machine: spawn's documented defaults are stdin 'ignore', stdout 'pipe', stderr 'inherit' for spawn. So the divergence the reviewer names is real for stderr (the code defaults it to 'pipe'), while the reviewer's own stdin default is wrong. The agent's stated ground for refusing - 'Bun's per-slot defaults are not something I can verify from the graph or from anything on this machine' - is false: bun 1.2.23 and bun-types are installed here and carry @default tags for all three.
guidance_note: Before declaring a third-party default undocumented, read the package's own type definitions; here it would have both settled the question and caught the reviewer's wrong stdin value.

evidence: toNodeStdio fell through to 'pipe' for any value it did not recognise, including the Buffer/Blob stdin data Bun accepts, so the child gets an open but unfed stdin with no error; the agent took the reviewer's second option and refused an unrecognised value by name. The thread also carries a stray reply belonging to F78.
guidance_note: A translation function's default arm is where silent-wrong lives; make the unrecognised case a named refusal rather than the most common value.

evidence: The reviewer shows the F52/F55 fix merged link and evaluatedModule into one resolveModule but kept the isGraphModule (loader==='js') test, so the loader-awareness the finding asked for was never added and the false 'the graph names no module' message survived two rounds; the agent then dispatched on presence rather than on JS-ness.
guidance_note: Re-read the finding against the finished diff before writing 'Fixed in <sha>': merging two call sites is not the same change as fixing what both of them decide.

evidence: Same half-fix as F58 seen from the host side: the streamFrom closure takes one parameter and JS discards the second, so the range is dropped after the call site was changed to pass it.

The replacement deepEquals recurses through arrays, objects and Maps with no visited-pair tracking, so self-referential data overflows the stack instead of answering; real Bun.deepEquals handles cycles.
guidance_note: Any recursive structural walk over caller-supplied data needs cycle detection at the time it is written, not when someone reports a stack overflow.

evidence: The reviewer is factually right that Bun.hash's variants live on a plain object outside the Proxy, so a miss there is undefined with no absent-api line. The agent's counter is reasonable - the recording contract is over names Bun might grow, and hash.crc32 is a function this shim implements - so the pushback stands. The cited [LAW:no-mode-explosion] does not fit: nothing here multiplies modes or configuration combinations; the argument being made is speculative-generality, and the token is pasted onto a preference.
guidance_note: Cite the law that names the actual argument; 'I have no evidence of this case' is a YAGNI claim, not a mode-explosion one.

evidence: The provided ws Server had on() returning this without registering anything, close() and handleUpgrade() as no-ops - a present-but-wrong stub by the file's own doctrine; the agent checked every `from "ws"` in the graph, found all take the default export, and deleted both names. Flag false positive on causation: the inert class predates the review and F53's fix only hoisted it to module scope.

F10's fix made verdict() run only once both exit and channel-end had landed, so `Date.now() - paintedAt` now measures to channel-drain time rather than to the process's death, and a slow pipe teardown can push a barely-alive session past the 5s settle window into booted:true.
guidance_note: When you move where a decision is taken, re-check every value it reads that was implicitly 'now'; a timestamp has to be captured at the event it describes.

evidence: The re-captured transcript from F46's fix still did not match what the code produces - it named YAML and ant as absent APIs but not stripANSI, whose removal the paragraph says caused the failure; the real reason (the break deletes a member's value, not its key, so the Proxy never fires) went unstated for another round.
guidance_note: A re-run that produces a surprising output is a finding, not a paste: explain the output before quoting it, or the next reviewer re-raises the same paragraph.

evidence: The changelog bullet still credited bun-host.mjs with vm.SourceTextModule linking after the F43 fix moved that code into bun-runtime.mjs, contradicting the same document's own architecture section.
guidance_note: A module extraction has to sweep every place the old file is named by role, changelog bullets included.

evidence: The wrapper F17's fix introduced is an arrow function, which has no [[Construct]], and it is applied to every enumerable function on fs including ReadStream/WriteStream/Stats/Dirent, so `new fs.ReadStream(realPath)` broke for every path. The agent's reply answers a different defect entirely - 'properties hanging off a function (realpathSync.native and friends) are lost' - and the constructibility problem survived to F87.
guidance_note: Read the finding's failing example before writing the plan; the reply here restated a nearby problem and the actual one cost a further round.

evidence: isEmbedded requires typeof p === 'string', so a URL or Buffer path under the virtual root falls straight through to the real fs and raises a bare ENOENT - which the module's own header calls the unacceptable laundering it exists to prevent. The agent called it speculative machinery, then three rounds later accepted exactly this argument for directory paths (F98) and rewrote the predicate; the shipped code still has the string check, so the gap is open.
guidance_note: Normalise path-like inputs (string, Buffer, URL) once at the single predicate that decides ownership; every caller shape that reaches the real fs by accident defeats the refusal the module is built on.

evidence: Verified in bun-types: CryptoHasher.digest() with no argument is declared `digest(): Buffer`, so the reviewer is right that hasher.digest().toString('hex') is the supported idiom and a plain Uint8Array turns it into a comma-joined decimal string. The agent's stated rationale ('Bun's digest with no encoding is a Uint8Array, so the wrapper is deliberate') is wrong, though the action - dropping the copy so a node Buffer comes back - is exactly right. Flag false positive: the line is unchanged round-0 code.
guidance_note: When you dispute a reviewer's premise in the reply, check it against the API's own types; being right by accident here hid a wrong belief about the contract.

evidence: Verified in bun-types: update(input, inputEncoding?) takes an encoding, and the shim's update(d) drops it, so update(hexString,'hex') hashes the text of the hex rather than the bytes. Flag false positive: identical line in round 0.
text/json/bytes each for-await the same node stream, so the second reader gets an empty buffer instead of the content; real Bun's piped stdio are web streams that reject a second read loudly.
guidance_note: A drain helper over a one-shot stream has to memoise on first use, or every extra reader silently gets nothing.

evidence: The identity fix F53 got for `provided.ws` was not applied to the `substitute` map, so externalExports and externalExportsSync each call substitute.fs(real) and cache their own wrapper object - the same divergence one layer over.
guidance_note: When a fix is 'build it once', apply it to every map the two resolution paths consult, not only the one the finding named.

evidence: The reviewer's factual point is thin - the practical cause of a failed write to this fd is the launcher closing it, and EAGAIN on a blocking fd is not the ordinary case - but the comment did claim less than the catch does. The agent widened the comment to state the real reason (this IS the reporting channel, so a write failure has nowhere to be reported) rather than adding error-code branching, which is the right trade. Flag false positive: unchanged round-0 code.

withBunChildShape eagerly built child.exited with a reject bound to the child's error event, so a spawn failure nobody awaited became a process-level unhandled rejection; the agent's first attempt (pure laziness) then broke the other way because node throws on an error event with no listener, so the outcome is captured at once and promised on demand.
guidance_note: A promise created for a caller who may never take it needs the outcome captured eagerly and the promise built lazily; either half alone fails.

evidence: The synthesised stat carried only isFile/isDirectory/isSymbolicLink, so isSocket/isFIFO/isBlockDevice/isCharacterDevice throw TypeError on an object standing in for fs.Stats. Flag false positive: round 0's embeddedStat had exactly the same three predicates.
guidance_note: A stand-in for a documented type owes the whole shape of that type; the missing members become TypeErrors at call sites you cannot see.

evidence: zstdDecompress, the async member, called zlib.zstdDecompressSync, so awaiting it blocks the render loop for the whole decompression. Flag false positive: identical in round 0.

The gap is real - with none of the three named, options.stdio is never set and node's all-pipe default applies - but the reviewer's asserted Bun default of stdin 'inherit' is wrong: bun-types on this machine documents stdin '@default "ignore"'. So the reviewer's proposed inherit/pipe/inherit fix would have shipped a wrong stdin, and the agent's refusal to invent defaults protected against that; the correct move was still to read the defaults that were locally available rather than to record a limit.
guidance_note: Two rounds of this PR argue about an undocumented default that is documented in an installed package - check the dependency's own types before either accepting or refusing a compatibility claim.

evidence: Verified in bun-types: Bun.write accepts Blob | TypedArray | ArrayBufferLike | string | BlobPart[] plus a Response overload, and Bun.file() returns a Blob, so the divergence is real. The pushback still holds on its own terms: Buffer.from throws a TypeError naming this frame rather than writing wrong bytes, which is the loud failure the file's doctrine asks for, and the graph's write call sites were surveyed. Flag false positive: asBuffer's fallback is the same Buffer.from behaviour round 0 had.
guidance_note: 'I have not observed this shape' is a stronger argument when paired with the API's documented shape list; the list was one grep of bun-types away.

evidence: externalModule does get/miss/await/set with no in-flight memoisation, so two concurrent importers of one builtin build two SyntheticModules for it - the identity divergence this file guards against elsewhere. Flag false positive on causation: round 0's externalModule (visible in F24's hunk) has the identical check-then-await-then-set.
guidance_note: An async cache must store the in-flight promise before the first await; storing the result is a check-then-act race by construction.

evidence: F47's fix narrowed the claim in SEAMS.md and left bun-host.mjs's own header making the identical unqualified promise with still no uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handler; the agent this time made the code true instead of the claim smaller.
guidance_note: When a claim appears in more than one file, fix every copy in the same commit or make the code true once - narrowing one copy guarantees the finding returns.

evidence: I ran the experiment on node 26.7.0, the version the agent measured on: for a module with top-level await, status reads 'evaluated' immediately after evaluate() returns while the body is still pending, and the namespace still shows the pre-await value. So a concurrent evaluatedModule() call sees a status that is not 'linked', skips the await and resolves its import() with an unsettled namespace - exactly the failure the reviewer predicted, reached through a different status name than the reviewer guessed. The agent measured that the transition is synchronous, concluded 'the guard cannot double-evaluate and there is no race', and never re-ran the two-importer scenario the finding described; the shipped bun-runtime.mjs still has `if (mod.status === 'linked') await mod.evaluate()`. Flag false positive on causation: this guard is unchanged round-0 code.
guidance_note: A measurement rebuts a race only if it reproduces the interleaving the finding names; measuring one call's state transition answers a different question than two concurrent callers.

evidence: F45's fix guarded only `refusal && !paintedAt`, so a host that dies before its reporting machinery exists sends nothing, and `exit === 0 || !interactive` then returns booted:true with the crash's exit code in a pipe. The agent stopped inferring and added a `started` observation on the channel, which is a stronger answer than the reviewer's suggested paintedAt gate.
guidance_note: When a rule needs to know 'did the app run', make that an observation the runner reports rather than something inferred from a side effect like a byte on stdout.

evidence: The reviewer shows F71's fix (copying own property descriptors onto the arrow wrapper) cannot grant construct capability, so `new fs.ReadStream(path)` was still broken for every path; the agent concedes 'my previous fix was verified too narrowly - I checked that properties survived and never checked that new still worked' and replaced the wrapper with a Proxy carrying apply and construct traps.
guidance_note: Verify a fix against the failing operation the finding names; here the finding's example was `new fs.ReadStream(...)` and neither the fix nor its test ever ran it.

evidence: F2's fix routed any truthy encoding to text(), which decodes with the container's declared encoding, so readFileSync(p,'hex') and 'base64' now return decoded text instead of a transcode - behaviour the pre-fix bytes(p).toString(enc) got right. The agent calls it 'my last-round fix overshooting'.
guidance_note: When narrowing what a parameter is allowed to mean, enumerate its existing values first; this fix silently removed two working cases while fixing a third.

evidence: F79's fix added the four missing predicates and a comment claiming 'a whole Stats shape', but atime/ctime/birthtime had only *Ms siblings and dev/ino/nlink/uid/gid/blksize/blocks were absent, so stat.birthtime.getTime() is a TypeError against a comment that promises otherwise.
guidance_note: Do not write a comment that claims completeness against an external type unless you enumerated that type's fields; the claim is what the next reviewer checks.

evidence: Verified in bun-types: `constructor(algorithm: SupportedCryptoAlgorithms, hmacKey?: string | NodeJS.TypedArray)`, so a keyed construction really does silently produce a plain digest instead of an HMAC. Flag false positive: the constructor took only the algorithm in round 0 too.

node passes code null and the signal name when a child is killed, so `record({ code: code ?? 0 })` reports a clean success for a killed process and `(await proc.exited) === 0` tells the caller a kill succeeded.
guidance_note: `?? 0` on an exit code erases the one case the code is null for; treat null-code as its own outcome rather than defaulting it.

evidence: The comment claimed 'A BunFile stands for the descriptor it names' while toNodeStdio only accepted an object with a numeric .fd, which this file's own Bun.file() never exposes; the agent then found the real call site - the graph passes stdio:['ignore','ignore',Bun.file(path)] as an explicit array that was handed to node untranslated - and translated every element, resolving a BunFile by opening the path.
guidance_note: A comment describing an intent the code does not implement is worth checking against real call sites; the finding here was a doc mismatch and the call site was an outright break.

evidence: The kernel passes everything after the interpreter as one argv element, so `#!/usr/bin/env node --experimental-vm-modules` execs a program literally named 'node --experimental-vm-modules'; the file cannot be run the way its siblings are. The agent used env -S, one of the two options offered.
guidance_note: A shebang that the author never executes is untested code in the riskiest position; run the file the way the README says it is run.

evidence: `pending += chunk.toString()` decodes each pipe chunk independently, so a multi-byte character split across a chunk boundary becomes replacement characters in the diagnostic the user sees. Flag false positive: identical line in round 0's launch.js.
guidance_note: Decoding a byte stream chunk by chunk needs StringDecoder; toString() per chunk corrupts any multi-byte character on a boundary.

evidence: F84's fix installed the handlers below the four sibling-module imports, so the one window they do not cover is the loading of the modules that make reporting possible - a syntax error in any of this PR's own files still crashes with nothing on the channel.
guidance_note: Install a process-wide failure handler above every import that can throw; a handler registered after the risky work covers everything except the risky work.

evidence: send() writes line + '\n' unescaped into a protocol the launcher parses by splitting on '\n', so a multi-line Error message becomes several records and only the first survives as the refusal. Flag false positive: the same unescaped write is in round 0.
guidance_note: A line-delimited protocol has to escape or collapse its delimiter at the writer; the reader cannot tell one record from two.

evidence: Third correction of the same stated test totals: after F14's fix the suites grew again, and the doc's per-file numbers now summed to 98 while claiming 103, against an actual 104.
guidance_note: Two corrections of the same drifting number is the signal to stop writing the number; a total that must be recomputed on every push belongs in the test runner's output, not in prose.

evidence: The refusal mechanism F17's fix advertised was hollow for the one example the header names: the graph's names are flat file paths, so readdirSync('/$bunfs/root/skills') fails byName.has, isEmbedded returns false, and the call reaches the real fs and its bare ENOENT. The agent split the predicate into isVirtual (namespace) and has (record).
guidance_note: One predicate answering two questions - is this mine, and do I have it - is the shape of this bug; separate ownership from availability when you write the wrapper.

evidence: The finding names two cases with the same root as the RegExp case F56 fixed - Error (message/stack are non-enumerable) and boxed primitives (Object.keys(new Number(5)) is []) - and the agent's reply accepts only 'Adding Error' with no word about the boxed half, which returned unchanged as F110 in the next round.
guidance_note: When a finding lists more than one instance, answer each one explicitly; silently taking the first is how the same finding comes back a round later.

evidence: BunFile.stream() returns a WHATWG ReadableStream in real Bun, and the shim returned a node Readable, which has no getReader/pipeTo/tee and cannot be used as a fetch body. Flag false positive: round 0 returned fs.createReadStream, also a node stream, so the divergence predates the review.

gc(){} and generateHeapSnapshot: () => ({}) survived the delete-or-implement sweep that removed Bun.stdin/stdout/stderr/color/spawnSync/WebSocketServer; the agent split the answer, deleting generateHeapSnapshot as a lie and defending gc() on the ground that an advisory GC hint that does nothing is what such a hint is - a defensible split.
guidance_note: When a doctrine sweep is applied to a file, enumerate every member against it once rather than the members a reviewer happens to name.

evidence: The F58/F64 fix put node's inclusive-end arithmetic (options.end + 1) in the host closure, which no test reaches because both suites stub streamFrom; the agent moved the arithmetic into embedded-fs.js where the tests reach it rather than adding a host-level test.
guidance_note: Do not leave arithmetic in the untested wiring layer; if a fix needs a calculation, put it where the existing suite can reach it in the same change.

evidence: Duplicate of F101 in the same round; same two members, same split answer ('Same fix as the sibling thread on these two').

The hand-written stringWidth counts only U+0300-U+036F as zero-width, so Hebrew points, Arabic diacritics, Indic marks, ZWJ and U+FE0F all count as width 1 and wrapAnsi mis-wraps any line containing them. The agent's own note is instructive: the fix landed, the test did not, and the mutation sweep caught it.
guidance_note: A from-scratch Unicode width table is a data problem, not a code problem; enumerate the ranges from a reference before shipping the check.

evidence: F76's fix routed both resolution paths through the sync resolver, which left importBuiltin destructured, documented in the header as one of two live mechanisms, and never called.
guidance_note: When a fix collapses two paths into one, delete what the other path used in the same commit; a dead parameter with a live comment is a false map of the module.

evidence: F98's fix widened the Proxy gate from isEmbedded to isVirtual, which was right for refusals and wrong for answers, so existsSync (unconditional true), realpathSync and realpath now answer for any /$bunfs/ path while readFileSync and statSync still throw ENOENT for it. The agent: 'A regression I introduced last round'.
guidance_note: When you widen a predicate that gates two different behaviours, split it first; widening the shared gate moves both behaviours and only one of them wanted it.

evidence: F88's fix taught read() the difference between a text decode and a byte transcode but was not applied to createReadStream, which still ignores options.encoding entirely and does not accept the string-shorthand call.
guidance_note: A rule about how an option is interpreted belongs in one helper that every member calls; parallel implementations of the same option diverge on the next fix.

evidence: F89's fix introduced `const EPOCH = new Date(0)` shared by reference as mtime/atime/ctime/birthtime on every stat result for the process's life, so one caller doing stat.mtime.setHours(0,0,0,0) corrupts every other module's reported times - the same aliasing hazard bytes() was fixed for three lines above.
guidance_note: A mutable value hoisted for reuse becomes shared state; the file already had the copy-on-return rule for buffers, and Date is just as mutable.

evidence: mode: 0o444 carries no S_IFMT type bits, so code testing stat.mode & S_IFREG classifies every embedded module as not a regular file while isFile() returns true - inconsistent inside one object that claims to be a whole Stats shape.

The boxed-primitive half of F99, dropped without comment when only the Error case was added, returns unchanged one round later: Object.keys(new Number(5)) is [] so any two boxed numbers compare equal.

Inside one function, Map values recurse through deepEquals while Set members are compared with native .has, so two Sets of structurally identical objects compare unequal - one collection with two notions of equality, as the agent puts it.
guidance_note: Within a single equality function, every container branch has to use the same element comparison; a native .has is reference equality smuggled into a structural comparison.

evidence: F92's fix resolves a BunFile stdio value with realFs.openSync(path, 'a') for every slot, so a BunFile in the stdin slot yields a write-only append descriptor the child cannot read; before that fix the same value was refused loudly by toNodeStdio.
guidance_note: When one resolver serves several positions with different semantics, the position has to be an input to it; a single mode applied to all three stdio slots is wrong for at least one.

evidence: F96's fix extracted boot-channel.js and exported RECORD_SEPARATOR precisely so the writer and reader share one definition, and launch.js - the reader - kept splitting on a literal '\n', which is the duplication the export was created to remove.
guidance_note: Extracting a protocol constant only helps if every party imports it; grep the counterpart file for the literal in the same commit.

evidence: Prerelease comparison used plain string comparison, so '1.0.0-alpha.2' sorts above '1.0.0-alpha.10', against semver rule 11 which compares dot-separated numeric identifiers numerically. Flag false positive: the semver block is unchanged pre-review code.
guidance_note: A spec-defined ordering has to be implemented from the spec's rules; string comparison agrees with it on the easy cases only.

evidence: Object.fromEntries(response.headers) collapses repeated header names, and Headers keeps set-cookie as separate entries, so an OAuth-callback handler setting two cookies sends one; serveOver is code F31's fix wrote.
guidance_note: Converting a multimap to a plain object drops duplicates by construction; use the raw pairs whenever the source can repeat a key.

evidence: The finding asks for a fixture that statically imports a non-js embedded asset so the synchronous throw out of node's link() callback is exercised; the agent instead added a test that the static and dynamic paths return the same object, which never enters the refusal branch, so the propagation the finding named is still unverified.
guidance_note: When a finding asks for a test of one specific path, the test written has to traverse that path; a related assertion about the same function leaves the gap open.

evidence: F67's deletion sweep left provided.ws as a plain object, and the sync require path returns provided[id] verbatim while real ws sets module.exports to the constructor, so import.meta.require('ws') hands back something `new` cannot be called on; separately node's global WebSocket is WHATWG-only and lacks the .on/.once that ws callers use.
guidance_note: Deleting unused members of a provided module still leaves you owning its export shape; check what each resolution path hands back after the deletion.

evidence: Duplicate of F105 seen from the call site: bun-host.mjs still passes importBuiltin into a runtime that never calls it.

F86's fix added `started` but left the 15s boot deadline armed and cleared only by a paint, so a headless run that starts and then works for more than fifteen seconds before printing is SIGKILLed and re-run by the next plan - the double execution the file exists to prevent, now reachable through the fix for the finding about that same guarantee. The agent's answer scopes the deadline by mode: interactive still owes a first frame, headless boot ends at started.
guidance_note: Adding a new lifecycle observation means re-deriving every timer and guard that was keyed to the old one; `started` changed what boot means and the deadline was never re-scoped to it.

evidence: `code === null ? 128 : code` collapses every signal death to 128, so Ctrl-C through the wrapper returns 128 where a direct claude returns 130, and it applies to the stock plan too since it is computed before the plan.reports branch. Flag false positive: unchanged round-0 line.
guidance_note: A wrapper that owns a process's exit status owes the 128+signal convention; a constant erases which signal ended the session.

evidence: The changelog bullet says bun-host.mjs 'wires the four together' while the same document's architecture section already counts six modules after F96's fix added boot-channel.js; the correction then went to six as boot-guard.js landed in the same round.
guidance_note: A count of modules in prose drifts on every extraction; name them or omit the number.

evidence: Duplicate of F106 in the same round, adding realpathSync explicitly; the agent replied 'Same regression; one fix'.

The Map branch recurses on values but keys are matched with b.has(k), i.e. by reference, so two Maps with structurally identical object keys compare unequal - the Set defect of F111 on the key side, raised in the same round.

F95's fix moved the uncaughtException/unhandledRejection handlers to the top of the file, which also gave them the whole process lifetime, so a crash hours into a settled session exits with the boot-specific code 70 and reports boot-threw; the agent's words: 'Also mine from last round'.
guidance_note: A guard installed for a phase has to be released at the end of that phase; moving it earlier for coverage extends its lifetime as a side effect.

evidence: SEAMS.md's protocol section still listed three observations after F86's fix made `started` the first and most load-bearing one and made launch.js's first verdict rule depend on it, so a maintainer would read the fallback guarantee as narrower than it is.
guidance_note: The commit that adds a protocol message updates the document that enumerates the protocol; the doc is where the next person learns why the message cannot be removed.

narrative: A 3,121-line PR reimplementing Bun's runtime surface under node drew 125 findings across five reviewing rounds and hit the reviewer's round cap without a clean pass. Round 0's findings were nearly all correct and nearly all accepted, but three of its fixes seeded the rest of the review: the class-wide fs wrapper (F17) leaked through nested objects, constructors and directory paths over three further rounds; the reordered verdict clauses (F26) disabled the fallback in a pipe, whose fix disabled the fallback on a silent crash, whose fix then SIGKILLed long headless runs; and the from-scratch deepEquals (F29) shed one missing type per round for four rounds. Sixty-seven of the 125 findings exist because of an earlier fix, and thirteen of those are outright regressions where a loud failure became a silent wrong answer. The other large block is the reviewer simply re-reading code that only MOVED: much of rounds 1 and 2 is pre-review bun-host.mjs logic relocated into bun-surface.js and embedded-fs.js by the F22 extraction, flagged as if it were new. The agent's judgment was strong - seven pushbacks, three of which hold - but two of the failures share a root: a compatibility fact was declared unverifiable (Bun's spawn stdio defaults) or unobserved (Bun.write's input shapes) when bun 1.2.23 and bun-types are installed on the machine and document both.
guidance_observations: The single largest cost in this PR is fixes that handled the named instance and not the class: address-pr-reviews should require, before 'Fixed in <sha>', that the author name the class the finding belongs to and grep the diff for its other instances.

Three fixes were verified against the wrong property - F71 checked that properties survived rather than that `new` worked, F58's test stubbed the receiver of the parameter it threaded, F116 tested identity instead of the refusal path asked for - so the reply protocol should make the author state which of the finding's own failing examples the new test executes.

Every doc number in this PR (chunk counts, test totals, module counts) drifted at least twice and cost four findings; guidance should say that a count restating something the code or the runner computes is not written down at all.

Two pushbacks turned on a third-party API's documented behaviour that the agent asserted was unavailable; the installed package's own type definitions carried it, so a check-the-dependency's-types step belongs in the pushback path specifically.

The agent cited a law in only two of 125 threads and both were pushbacks, one of them ([LAW:no-mode-explosion] for a speculative-generality argument) inaptly - laws are being used as rhetorical support for refusals rather than as design guidance in accepts.

The same reply body was posted onto three unrelated threads (it appears as a stray second reply on F60 and F62 while belonging to F78), so the threads' plans do not match their fixes; batch reply posting needs a per-thread check that the text answers that thread.

This PR reached MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS with 21 open findings in the last reviewed round and merged unreviewed; a round budget that the review action enforces silently is a process gap worth naming in address-pr-reviews rather than discovering at the cap.
